target_customer: Growth and product marketing teams at subscription and consumer software companies (customers named at launch: InVision, theSkimm)
problem: Marketers could not tell which users were likely to convert or which behaviors actually caused conversion without running many slow A/B tests.
business_model: Self-serve SaaS subscription (launch pricing from 499 USD per month)

founders.name: Bilal Mahmood
prior_employers: Optimizely (product manager, later described as leading data science)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2018-02) calls him a former Optimizely product manager; Amplitude calls him head of Optimizely data science. Wikipedia lists him as CEO until March 2020.

founders.name: Eric Pollmann
prior_employers: Google (Ads engineer; first SRE on Google Ads per Amplitude)

technical_complexity.rationale: Automated machine learning over customers' event data pulled from Segment, Heap and Optimizely, with a patent-pending causal inference engine added in 2019; standard ML engineering with hard modeling parts, done by a very small team.

defensibility.rationale: The causal-modeling method was described as patent-pending, but the product depended on customers' data in third-party analytics pipes and a larger analytics vendor could add predictions as a feature, which is what Amplitude did.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amplitude bought ClearBrain in March 2020 to add predictions to its analytics product, its first acquisition; free-plan users were given until end of April 2020 to migrate.

market_need_then: Marketing teams wanted to personalise and retarget using predicted purchase intent; TechCrunch (2018-02) described ClearBrain as a way to avoid heavy manual A/B testing, and Amplitude later described the same need for predicting which features and campaigns drive revenue.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, product-led announcements; launch coverage emphasised team credentials and humility; the YC description mentions bowling and D&D

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, mascot or community found; the name is descriptive-leaning but memorable enough, with no sourced effect.

pivots.from: Predictive audience and retargeting platform for growth marketing
pivots.to: Causal analytics product (early access Aug 2019, wider launch Oct 2019)
pivots.why: Founder said correlation-based analytics tools miss causal drivers; per TechCrunch 2019 coverage as summarised in search results.

outcome_analysis: ClearBrain raised a small 1.2M USD seed at YC W18, sold a self-serve predictive product to growth teams, and in 2019 moved to causal analytics, but the only other round found is an unverified 2M USD seed. In March 2020 Amplitude acquired it, absorbing the ML team into its product; terms are undisclosed, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing is not public. Founders from Google Ads and Optimizely data teams gave credibility, yet a bigger analytics incumbent was the natural buyer of the wedge.
notes: A second seed of about 2.0M USD in 2019-08 (Harrison Metal, Menlo Ventures) appears only on Seedtable, an aggregator, and the Seedtable page returned 403 when fetched; recorded here as unverified, not as a round. CB Insights gives a conflicting 120K USD total. TechCrunch 2018 named no direct competitors (Segment, Heap, Optimizely are data sources), so the list is empty rather than filled from today's market. Founding year 2016 is from Wikipedia as quoted in search results; YC lists no year. Directory status Acquired agrees with the exit.
